teaser: Knowing when to stop is the hard part for people and agents: what experience gives people, and the constraints that give agents the same perspective.
core_idea: Knowing when to stop is the hardest call in most work: for people it comes from perspective, knowing the attackers, the phase of the business, the bottleneck and what good enough looks like, which is much of what seniority is; good teams without it defend against movie plots or hit every KPI without moving the business; agents have the same problem by design because their range is the feature, so they keep going; the answer for both is constraints that carry perspective, direction, a mandate, memory with the bigger picture, graphs that narrow the scope, a stop named in advance, one kind of work per step, a reviewer with agency, and shipping often enough to see whether it mattered.

nodes.label: Variability is the feature
nodes.summary: Agents can go in every direction; that is what makes them useful, and why they need direction.

nodes.label: What seniority gives you
nodes.summary: The bigger picture: strategy, the real risks, moving between tactical and strategic.

nodes.label: Debating whether GUIDs are random enough
nodes.summary: Teams that automated away bug classes then defended against a movie plot; 122 random bits.

nodes.label: Giving permission to take risks
nodes.summary: Perspective, not common sense: technically possible, and it does not matter here.

nodes.label: Every KPI hit, needle still
nodes.summary: Teams reverse-engineer metrics; when a measure becomes a target it stops measuring.

nodes.label: Which phase are you in?
nodes.summary: A Wardley map says whether polish is right or waste, and where the bottleneck is.

nodes.label: Art is knowing when to stop
nodes.summary: Good enough and diminishing returns; shipping and observability as the feedback loop.

nodes.label: Why it is harder for agents
nodes.summary: A wide range of skills and no natural limit: fix the small thing, then the bigger one, then all twenty.

nodes.label: Work expands to fill the team
nodes.summary: Parkinson 1955; any entity that can do work, put in a team, will find work.

nodes.label: Constraints that carry perspective
nodes.summary: FIRE rather than draconian rules: direction, mandate, memory, graphs, a named stop, one step, review, shipping.

quotes.text: An entity that can go anywhere has no natural reason to stop anywhere.
quotes.why: Why agents need the stop designed in.

quotes.text: What I found myself doing, in that meeting and in many others across the business, was giving people permission to take risks.
Each puts the bigger picture where the decision is made, which is what lets a person, or an agent, decide that the next thing is not worth doing.
